c.tagline: Australia's beach-holiday capital of surf, high-rises, theme parks, and green hinterland.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered (GC Cabs is the main operator); a booking fee applies for phone or app bookings and airport pickups add a surcharge.

emergency.note: 000 is the primary emergency number; 112 also works from any mobile and 106 is the text-based line for the deaf or speech-impaired.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Main Beach: Tedder Avenue Main Beach Gold Coast

avoid.reason: The Surfers Paradise nightlife strip gets rowdy with alcohol-fuelled trouble late at night, especially during Schoolies Week; always swim between the flags on patrolled beaches.

hood_desc: The high-rise heart of the Gold Coast, where a golden surf beach meets Cavill Avenue's shops, bars, and nightclubs; brash, busy, and the classic first-timer base for beach days and late nights.
A more polished beachside district just south of Surfers, home to The Star casino, the Pacific Fair mall, and a strip of acclaimed restaurants and cafes; upscale dining with the tram at the door.
An exclusive enclave between the Broadwater and the ocean, known for chic Tedder Avenue, the marina at Marina Mirage, and Sea World nearby; refined, low-key, and moneyed.
A laid-back, hip surf town wrapped around a headland national park, with a famous point break, buzzing James Street eateries, and a village feel; the coast's coolest, most relaxed pocket.
The southernmost twin-town beach community by the NSW border and the airport, with classic surf beaches at Kirra and Rainbow Bay; nostalgic, uncrowded, and family-friendly.
lodging: The Star Grand at The Star Gold Coast
Sheraton Grand Mirage Resort Gold Coast
Komune Resort & Beach Club Gold Coast

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Australia.

transit.hours: The G:link tram runs roughly 5am to midnight (24 hours on peak weekends), with buses on similar hours; Queensland Rail Gold Coast line trains connect the western suburbs to Brisbane.
transit.note: One TransLink network covers the G:link light rail running along the coast from Helensvale through Surfers Paradise and Broadbeach, the Kinetic Surfside bus network, and the Gold Coast heavy-rail line to Brisbane.
transit.pay: Tap on and off with a go card or a contactless Visa, Mastercard, or Amex card or phone; since 2024 every journey across South East Queensland is a flat 50-cent fare, with transfers included.

bus: Coaches to Brisbane, Byron Bay and northern NSW

Taxi or rideshare to Surfers Paradise (25-35 min)

food.name: Fish and chips
food.desc: Beer-battered or grilled local snapper, flathead and whiting with hot chips, eaten out of paper on the sand at sunset.

places.name: Burleigh Heads Fishmongers
places.note: A stone's throw from the water; the surfer-and-local favourite for fresh, no-fuss fish and chips.

places.name: Charis Seafoods
places.note: Broadwater institution with a huge fresh-fish counter and a fry shop; feed the pelicans afterwards.

places.name: Miami Fish Market
places.note: Sustainably sourced fish plus battered Moreton Bay bugs, kingfish wings and whitebait.

food.name: Moreton Bay bug roll
food.desc: Sweet slipper-lobster tail, butter-poached and sriracha-glazed, stuffed into a soft roll - the Gold Coast's most copied dish.

places.name: Rick Shores
places.note: The original bug roll, served with your feet almost in the surf at Burleigh Pavilion.

places.name: The Tropic
places.note: Upstairs at Burleigh Pavilion for grilled bugs, sashimi and prawns with a full beach view.

places.name: Blowfish Ocean Grill + Bar
places.note: Bug rolls, an oyster and sashimi bar and towering seafood platters on Kurrawa Beach.

food.name: Smashed avocado brunch
food.desc: The full Aussie beach brunch: smashed avo on sourdough with feta, dukkah and poached eggs, ordered alongside a flat white.

places.name: Paddock Bakery
places.note: Queenslander cottage with a garden out back; the Gold Coast's most photographed brunch spot.

places.name: Elk Espresso
places.note: Long-running Burleigh cafe a block from the beach, big all-day brunch menu.

places.name: BSKT Cafe
places.note: Health-leaning beachside kitchen known for smashed avo, bowls and long weekend queues.

food.name: Lamington
food.desc: Queensland's own sponge square, dipped in chocolate and rolled in desiccated coconut, sometimes split with jam and cream.

places.name: Bam Bam Bakehouse
places.note: Cult pastry counter that riffs on the classic lamington alongside its famous croissants.

places.name: Dust Temple
places.note: Cafe and art space with a house cake cabinet; a relaxed southern-end coffee-and-cake stop.

places.name: Miami Marketta
places.note: Street-food warehouse market where local bakers sell sweets on Wednesday to Saturday nights.

food.name: Grilled Queensland prawns
food.desc: Wild-caught tiger and king prawns, sold cooked by the kilo off the trawlers or grilled with garlic butter.

places.name: Peters Fish Market
places.note: Waterfront fish market and fry shop; buy cooked prawns by the kilo and eat them on the Broadwater.

places.name: Omeros Bros Seafood Restaurant
places.note: Long-established Marina Mirage seafood house with a full display of the day's catch.

places.name: The Fish House
places.note: Upmarket Gold Coast Highway seafood room; simple charcoal-grilled prawns and reef fish.

food.name: Aussie meat pie
food.desc: Flaky pastry filled with chunky beef gravy, topped with tomato sauce - the classic Queensland roadside and footy-day feed.

places.name: Yatala Pies
places.note: Highway landmark baking pies on this site since the 1880s; the classic stop north of the city.

places.name: Paddock Bakery
places.note: House-baked pies and sausage rolls from the Gold Coast's best-known suburban bakery.

places.name: Bam Bam Bakehouse
places.note: Serious pastry work, including savoury pies, from a bakery with a genuine local following.

food.name: Flat white
food.desc: Australia's espresso-and-steamed-milk staple, poured from locally roasted beans; the Gold Coast takes its coffee seriously.

places.name: Blackboard Coffee
places.note: Small-batch roaster and cafe; a Burleigh benchmark for filter and espresso.

places.name: Canteen Coffee
places.note: Tiny, always-busy Burleigh hole-in-the-wall known purely for the quality of the pour.

places.name: BSKT Cafe
places.note: Roasts its own beans and serves them with a big beachside brunch menu.

food.name: Gold Coast craft beer
food.desc: The coast is Queensland's craft-brewing hub - hazy pale ales and XPAs poured metres from where they are made.

places.name: Balter Brewing
places.note: Surfer-founded brewery whose XPA is a national favourite; open taproom in an industrial estate.

places.name: Black Hops Brewing
places.note: Popular Burleigh taproom with rotating small-batch beers and food trucks.

places.name: Burleigh Brewing Co
places.note: The coast's pioneering craft brewery; big beer garden and long-running local following.

landmarks: Surfers Paradise Beach
Australia's most famous stretch of golden sand meets a skyline of glittering towers, with rolling surf breaks patrolled year-round between the flags.
SkyPoint Observation Deck (Q1 Tower)
Rocket 77 floors up one of the world's tallest residential towers for 360-degree views from the surf line to the hinterland ranges.
Burleigh Heads National Park
An oceanfront headland walk through rainforest and pandanus, overlooking one of the world's great point breaks and passing whales in season.
Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary
A heritage-listed sanctuary famed for its wild rainbow lorikeet feedings, koala encounters and conservation hospital in lush coastal bushland.
Snapper Rocks and the Superbank
At Coolangatta's southern tip, surfing's most mechanically perfect sand-bottom point break peels for kilometres past Rainbow Bay's golden crescent.
Warner Bros. Movie World
The flagship of the Gold Coast's theme-park strip delivers Hollywood stunt shows, DC superheroes and some of the southern hemisphere's biggest coasters.
The Spit and Main Beach
A low-rise peninsula of dunes and seaway walls where locals walk dogs at dawn, dolphins cruise the channel and Marina Mirage serves seafood.
Sea World
A marine mammal park and oceanarium on The Spit that grew out of a 1970s water-ski show, combining rides with dolphin, seal and shark exhibits tied to a wildlife rescue program.
Dreamworld
Australia's largest theme park and zoo in Coomera, known for the record-breaking Giant Drop tower, the country's oldest operating steel roller coaster, and native wildlife exhibits.
HOTA, Home of the Arts
A riverside arts precinct on Chevron Island with a contemporary gallery, an outdoor sculpture lawn and an amphitheatre hosting concerts, festivals and film screenings.

train.note: There are no international trains. The Queensland Rail Gold Coast line runs from Varsity Lakes, Robina, Nerang and Helensvale up to Brisbane (about 70-90 minutes); connect to the G:link tram at Helensvale for the beach suburbs. Book and tap on with a go card.

bus.note: No international buses. Greyhound and Premier run coaches down the Pacific Highway to Byron Bay and Sydney, and up to Brisbane; regional operators link the hinterland.

ferry.note: The Gold Coast has no scheduled passenger ferries to other cities; boating on the Broadwater and canals is by private craft, cruise, or water-taxi only.

half.name: Tamborine Mountain
half.blurb: A hinterland plateau of rainforest walks, the Skywalk, wineries, and the 'Gallery Walk' craft strip, about 45 minutes inland.

half.name: Springbrook National Park
half.blurb: Gondwana rainforest with waterfalls, the Natural Bridge cave, and a famous glow-worm colony.

full.name: Byron Bay
full.blurb: Australia's most easterly point, a boho beach town of lighthouse walks, surf, and markets about an hour south in NSW.

full.name: Lamington National Park
full.blurb: World-heritage rainforest of the McPherson Range, with tree-top walks and Antarctic beech forest at O'Reilly's and Binna Burra.

full.name: Brisbane
full.blurb: Queensland's riverside capital, an hour north by train or car, for South Bank, galleries, and city dining.
